title: Job 27
paragraphs: ¹ And Job continued his discourse and said, ² As God lives — who has denied me justice, and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul — ³ as long as I have breath within me and the breath of God is in my nostrils, ⁴ my lips will not speak falsehood and my tongue will not utter deceit. ⁵ God forbid that I should agree with you — till I die I will not renounce my integrity.

⁶ I hold fast to my righteousness and will not let it go; my conscience does not reproach me for any of my days. ⁷ May my enemy be as the wicked, and my adversary as the unrighteous. ⁸ For what hope does the godless man have when he is cut off, when God takes away his life? ⁹ Will God hear his cry when distress comes upon him? ¹⁰ Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at any time?

¹¹ I will teach you about the power of God; I will not hide what the Almighty has in store. ¹² You have all seen this yourselves — why then do you talk such empty nonsense? ¹³ This is the portion of a wicked man before God, the inheritance the Almighty gives to ruthless men: ¹⁴ If his children multiply, it is only for the sword; his offspring will never have enough to eat. ¹⁵ Those who survive him will be buried by the plague, and their widows will not mourn for them.

¹⁶ Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay, ¹⁷ what he stores up, the righteous will wear, and the innocent will divide his silver. ¹⁸ The house he builds is as flimsy as a moth's cocoon, like a shelter made by a watchman. ¹⁹ He lies down rich but will rise no more; when he opens his eyes, all is gone. ²⁰ Terror overtakes him like a flood; a tempest snatches him away in the night.

²¹ The east wind carries him off and he is gone, sweeping him away from his place. ²² It hurls itself at him without mercy as he flees headlong from its power. ²³ People clap their hands at him and hiss him away from his place.
